01 · How it works

From an address to a drawing set, in seven steps.

Each step is one tab in the tool. Everything you change carries through to every drawing, so the plans, elevations, 3D model and report always agree.

A-01 · Base Map

Start with your lot.

Search an address or tap a parcel

Every R1-1 lot in the city is on the map and already classified. Pick yours and the callout tells you right away whether a laneway house can go there — lane at the rear, nothing built behind the house — and why.

  • Search any civic address, or start from a test case
  • See viable lots, corner lots and through lots at a glance
  • A mini plan of the lot pops up in the corner
A-02 · Existing Lot

Know what you're working with.

Your lot, read from City data

The lot, the existing house and its yards are drawn as a plan, with the numbers that matter beside it: frontage, depth, site area, the buildable pocket and the floor area you're allowed.

  • Lot dimensions, area and orientation
  • Existing house footprint and setbacks
  • Laneway potential: the floor-area cap and the height limit
A-03 · Laneway House Drawings

Shape it to fit — parametrically.

Presets to start, then make it yours

Start from a single-storey cottage or a two-storey gable house, then size it exactly: drag the walls in the plans or use the sliders. The site plan, floor plans, all four elevations and the 3D model move together while ten by-law checks keep score.

  • Single or double storey, gable roof, any size the lot allows
  • Setbacks, separation, height, coverage and floor area checked live
  • Lane, left, right and street-side elevations with property lines
A-04 · Floor Plans

Make the rooms yours.

Rooms, furniture, windows and doors

Layouts are drawn to code at your size — a straight or switchback stair, an accessible washroom, kitchen, open living and bedrooms. Then customise: move walls, draw a room, add a door, drag and rotate furniture, and place windows from the rooms. Pick a window in the plan and the elevation beside it shows exactly where it lands.

  • Studio, 1-bed and 2-bed layouts — single or two storey
  • Drag walls, draw rooms, add or remove doors
  • Furniture library: sofas, tables, beds, desks and more
A-05 · Isometric Design View

See it in the neighbourhood.

Isometric with the sun path

A clean isometric of your lot and its neighbours, with callouts for the volumes and setbacks. Turn on the sun path for your exact location and play the day to see where the shadows fall.

  • Sun path for the lot's latitude, any day of the year
  • Shadows from the house, the laneway house, trees and neighbours
  • Export the view as a PNG
A-06 · Details

Choose the materials.

Cladding, roofing, trim and frames

Try light cedar below and dark metal above, a shingle or standing-seam roof, black or bronze frames. The rendered model updates instantly, with camera views from the street, the lane and the garden.

  • Twenty claddings, nine roofs, six trims, four frame colours
  • A different cladding for the upper floor
  • Material schedule for the drawing set
A-07 · Rendering

Render the view you want.

Your camera, your image

Orbit, pan and zoom the model until the angle is right, save it, and make a studio render right in the tool — no account or key needed. Have a Gemini key? Turn the same view into a photoreal or watercolour render.

  • Save as many camera views as you like
  • Studio render in seconds, offline
  • Choose which render goes in your report
Report

Take it with you.

Every drawing, one click

The report button builds a six-sheet A3 set: cover with the key figures, site and existing lot, floor plans, four elevations, views with your render and the sun path, and the compliance checks with a window and door schedule. Print it, save it as a PDF or download it.

  • Ready for a first conversation with the City or a designer
  • Cited by-law clauses on every check
  • Uses the render you picked
02 · Drawings

Drawings that look like drawings.

Plans, elevations and views come out in a consistent drafting style — hairlines, title blocks, scale bars and the same calm palette throughout.

04 · The rules

The rules it checks, as you design.

From the R1-1 District Schedule and the Missing Middle report, Appendix A, s.11.3.8 — each check cites its clause in the tool.

4.9 mSeparation from the main houses.11.3.8.6(a)
8.5 mMaximum building heights.11.3.8.4
0.9 mSetback from the rear lot lines.11.3.8.6(b)
1.2 mSetback from each side lot lines.11.3.8.6(c)
≤ 25 %Floor area, up to 186 m²s.11.3.8.2
≤ 50 %Site coverage with the laneway houses.11.3.8.5
9.8 mMinimum site widths.11.3.8.3
≤ 60 %Upper floor of the ground floorbrief rule
LaneVehicular access from a rear lanes.11.3.8.1
BCBCStairs: 200 mm rise, 255 mm tread, guards9.8
